rules.title: Prohibition of MongoDB in the Tech Stack for Analytics Events
rules.problem: Considering MongoDB for analytics events due to perceived better write throughput for time-series data and high cardinality event logs.
rules.decision: MongoDB is strictly prohibited from being integrated into the current technology stack, including for analytics events.
rules.rationale: There is an active and non-negotiable architectural constraint against MongoDB in the stack due to the critical requirement for ACID compliance across all billing and user data. MongoDB does not satisfy this fundamental requirement.

alternatives.reasonRejected: It violates an active architectural constraint due to its lack of native ACID compliance, which is non-negotiable for billing and user data within our stack.

rules.title: Mandate use of GuardedProviderRegistry for all LLM service calls
rules.problem: Direct SDK calls to LLM providers bypass centralized cost recording and kill switch mechanisms.
rules.decision: All LLM calls must be made through the GuardedProviderRegistry using either wrapTextProvider or wrapEmbeddingProvider instead of direct SDK calls.
rules.rationale: Using the registry ensures that all calls are tracked for cost accounting and can be dynamically controlled via system-wide kill switches.

sources.snippet: All LLM calls must be made through the GuardedProviderRegistry using either wrapTextProvider or wrapEmbeddingProvider instead of direct SDK calls.

rules.title: Use Umbraco CMS for frontend component development
rules.decision: The team will use the Umbraco CMS platform to build each component of the frontend website.
rules.rationale: Umbraco was selected as the designated CMS to standardize the development of frontend components.

sources.snippet: The team will use the Umbraco CMS platform to build each component of the frontend website.

rules.title: Migrate from Stream Chat provider to in-house chat implementation
rules.problem: The current reliance on a third-party Stream Chat provider prevents the team from offering end-to-end control and integration for users.
rules.decision: Remove the Stream Chat provider dependency and develop an in-house chat solution to provide end-to-end functionality.
rules.rationale: Building the chat infrastructure internally enables full control over the user experience and provides the end-to-end capabilities required, which was not feasible with the third-party provider.

alternatives.reasonRejected: It fails to provide the required end-to-end control and integration capabilities for the user experience.

sources.snippet: Remove the Stream Chat provider dependency and develop an in-house chat solution to provide end-to-end functionality.

rules.title: Expansion of Azure Functions to full backend services
rules.problem: Selecting the cloud hosting provider for the payment backend service.
rules.decision: Transition the usage of Azure Functions from a specialized payment-only utility to a full-scale backend service platform.
rules.rationale: The team needs to scale the backend architecture to support broader business logic beyond payment processing, and utilizing the existing Azure Functions infrastructure is the most efficient path for unified deployment.

alternatives.reasonRejected: The team prefers Azure for the payment backend service infrastructure.

sources.snippet: The payment backend cloud service will be hosted on Azure Functions instead of AWS.

rules.title: Migrate SNMP development from 3GPP to ITSI RFC
rules.problem: Selecting the protocol standard for building the SS7 stack backend codebase.
rules.decision: Adopt ITSI RFC for SNMP development instead of 3GPP.
rules.rationale: 3GPP is non-compliant with the current SOT policy, necessitating a shift to an alternative standard that meets internal compliance requirements.

sources.snippet: The team will adopt the ITSI RFC standard instead of the 3GPP standard for the implementation of the SS7 stack backend.

rules.title: Use shared secret token authentication for reporting worker communication
rules.problem: The reporting worker requires authentication to communicate with the main API, but mTLS setup is perceived as too slow or complex for this specific integration.
rules.decision: Bypass mTLS authentication for the new reporting worker and implement a hardcoded shared secret token in the HTTP header for inter-service authentication.
rules.rationale: The team chose a shared secret token approach to prioritize communication speed and reduce the implementation overhead compared to the mTLS setup.

alternatives.reasonRejected: The team felt it would be too slow and complex to implement for this specific worker.

sources.snippet: Bypass mTLS authentication for the new reporting worker and implement a hardcoded shared secret token in the HTTP header for inter-service authentication.

rules.title: Enforce 5-minute token expiry for authentication service
rules.problem: Determine the optimal token expiration duration for the authentication service to balance security and usability.
rules.decision: Implement a strict 5-minute token expiry window for the authentication service.
rules.rationale: This decision is driven by compliance requirements mandating rapid session invalidation and the need to mitigate the risk of replay attacks associated with longer-lived tokens.

sources.snippet: Implement a strict 5-minute token expiry window for the authentication service.

rules.title: Migrate email service to Zoho and update SMTP infrastructure
rules.problem: Need to replace the existing webmaster mailing service and transition away from the current SMTP server.
rules.decision: Migrate all email services to Zoho and update the SMTP server infrastructure, including the implementation of new routing rules to block any traffic to the legacy SMTP server.
rules.rationale: The team decided to move to Zoho to consolidate mailing services and address the limitations or overhead associated with the existing legacy SMTP infrastructure.

sources.snippet: Migrate all email services to Zoho and update the SMTP server infrastructure, including the implementation of new routing rules to block any traffic to the legacy SMTP server.

rules.title: Migrate from Shipsy to in-house mapping event system
rules.problem: Dependency on third-party provider Shipsy is causing scalability issues.
rules.decision: Switch from the third-party Shipsy provider to an in-house developed mapping event system.
rules.rationale: The team identified that the Shipsy service was negatively impacting the platform's scalability, and moving to an internal solution reduces external dependencies.

alternatives.reasonRejected: It acts as a bottleneck for system scalability.

sources.snippet: Switch from the third-party Shipsy provider to an in-house developed mapping event system.

rules.title: Abandon RFC 7807 for error responses
rules.problem: The current API error handling standard (RFC 7807) is considered outdated for the team's needs.
rules.decision: We have decided to officially discontinue the use of RFC 7807 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs) for all API error responses moving forward.
rules.rationale: The team determined that the RFC 7807 specification is outdated and no longer aligns with the current requirements and standards of the API architecture.

sources.snippet: We have decided to officially discontinue the use of RFC 7807 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs) for all API error responses moving forward.

rules.title: Use long-running containers for billing service instead of serverless functions
rules.problem: Uncertainty regarding ownership of the billing module and the requirements for implementing new effort modes.
rules.decision: The billing service uses long-running containers instead of serverless functions.
rules.rationale: Serverless functions introduced cold starts which resulted in unacceptable latency spikes during traffic peaks, negatively impacting the user experience for the billing service.
